name: Sealed cable end
summary: A cable end that is sealed and capped but not connected, such as a spare circuit or a cable laid for future use.
description: A sealed cable end shows a cable that terminates without connection, typically capped with a heat-shrink or cold-shrink end cap. It appears on network diagrams for spare circuits, cables laid ahead of future equipment, and cables isolated and left in the ground after a fault or diversion.

A capped cable may still be connected at its other end and therefore energised. The symbol does not tell you its state, so the reader must check the switching position at the source end before treating it as dead. Drawings should also note whether the cable is earthed for safety.
readingNotes: Check the far end to see whether the cable is energised.
Look for notes that the capped cable is earthed or isolated.
drawingChecklist: Note the energisation state of the capped cable.
Identify planned future use where known.
distinction: A sealed cable end has no connection; a sealing end is a termination connected to equipment or a line.
